prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2015 – Summary (under 500 words)

Vision
- Build a stronger, fairer, open UK by 2020: balanced budget by 2017/18, debt falling, sustainable growth, opportunity for all.
- Fund key services, protect rights, and lead a rapid transition to a low‑carbon economy.

Economy and industry
- Balanced approach to deficit reduction: no rises in income tax, NI, VAT or corporation tax rates; raise revenue from avoidance, banks, polluters and wealth.
- Double economy‑wide innovation spend; expand British Business Bank; boost SMEs and regional growth; devolve economic powers locally.
- Expand Green Investment Bank; legally target net‑zero emissions by 2050; 60% renewable electricity by 2030; end unabated coal by 2025; support CCS, storage and community energy.
- Major transport/digital upgrades: rail electrification, HS2, North strategy, East‑West Rail; broadband to 99.9%.

Tax, welfare, work and pensions
- Raise Personal Allowance to at least £12,500; clamp down on avoidance; levy on £2m+ properties.
- Childcare: towards 20 free hours for ages 2–4 and from 9 months for working parents; complete Tax‑Free Childcare.
- Roll out Universal Credit; reform sanctions; temporary 1% cap on working‑age benefits to 2017/18; tackle high rents; Living Wage in central government.
- Improve disability assessments; reform “bedroom tax” with medical/adaptation exemptions.
- Pensions: protect triple lock in law; complete single‑tier pension; strengthen auto‑enrolment; greater freedom over pension pots.

Consumers
- 24‑hour energy switching; smart meters with protections; inflation‑capped rail fares; curb Fixed Odds Betting Terminals.

Education and skills
- Protect funding from nursery to 19; maintain/extend Pupil Premium.
- Qualified teachers in every class; independent standards body; slim core curriculum incl. PSHE/sex & relationships education and RE.
- Leadership and teacher development; extend free school meals in primary as resources allow.
- Double firms hiring apprentices; expand Higher Apprenticeships/National Colleges; fairer HE access and finance review.
- Discount bus pass (16–21).

Health and care
- NHS free at point of use; at least £8bn extra by 2020; faster diagnostics/treatments.
- Mental health parity: waiting‑time standards, £500m extra, stronger crisis care, perinatal/children’s services.
- Integrate health and social care with pooled budgets by 2018; better GP access; stronger public health (smoking, alcohol, food).
- Carers’ package: £250 bonus, better rights; improve social care quality, training, pay.

Environment, farming and rural
- Five Green Laws: Nature; Zero Carbon Britain; Resource Efficiency/Zero Waste (70% recycling target); Green Transport (Low Emission Zones, EV push); Green Buildings.
- Protect and expand green space/coastal path; support sustainable farming, fair supply chains, animal welfare; flood resilience.
- Rural services: no Post Office closure programme; complete broadband; better buses.

Housing
- Build 300,000 homes a year; Garden Cities; public land development; Housing Investment Bank.
- Strengthen plan‑led system; prioritise brownfield; fair appeals.
- Affordable/rent‑to‑own/intermediate homes; protect private renters with multi‑year tenancies, fair fees.
- Home efficiency: Council Tax discount for upgrades; targets to reach EPC Band C.

Rights, justice, drugs, immigration
- Protect Human Rights Act; Digital Bill of Rights; Second Freedoms Act.
- Combat discrimination (women, BAME, LGBT+, disability); tackle hate crime.
- Replace PCCs with Police Boards; Victims’ Bill; focus on rehabilitation; presumption against short prison terms; drug policy modelled on Portugal for possession.
- Complete entry/exit checks; fair, faster asylum; welcome skilled migrants and students.

Democracy and devolution
- Votes at 16; STV for Westminster and local elections; Lords reform; party donations capped at £10k; constitutional convention.
- Implement Smith (Scotland), go beyond Silk (Wales); devolution on demand in England.

International
- Strongly pro‑EU with reform; back fair TTIP; clamp down on global tax avoidance.
- 0.7% aid maintained; lead on climate (50% EU cut by 2030); rules‑based foreign policy.
- SDSR with Single Security Budget; scale down to non‑continuous nuclear deterrence.
